body.x: Parallel Space Co., Ltd. (CEO Jieun Lee) announced its participation in CES 2025 in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 at the K-Startup Pavilion.

Through extensive in-house research and development, Parallel Space has established itself as a Spatial AI and Geometric Algorithms leader. The company offers software that automatically generates and converts point cloud data captured from real-world spaces into 3D graphics.

Its custom software, designed for applications like building defect inspections, facility management, and moving logistics, has demonstrated strong competitiveness in the spatial information sector. By focusing on rapid and accurate 3D automation solutions, Parallel Space aims to support digital transformation (DX) across various industries globally.
At CES 2025, Parallel Space will unveil its cutting-edge 3D reconstruction solution, P-Engine, which boasts extensive versatility across multiple industrial applications.

The solution is based on proprietary algorithms and AI technology, enabling fast and precise conversion of scanned data into 3D meshes. It is optimized for scanning large-scale industrial facilities, such as factories, and creating high-quality digital twins from the collected data.

Automating the 3D reconstruction process involves complex mathematical calculations and programming. Existing solutions often fail to meet essential technical standards, resulting in incomplete outputs that require manual intervention by 3D model designers. Additionally, the quality of digital twins has historically been influenced by designers’ skills and intuition, a persistent limitation within the industry. Parallel Space addresses these challenges with P-Engine, offering a high level of automation and technological distinction.

The company will also present P-BIM, a tool that compares lightweight 3D models reconstructed with P-Engine against BIM data. This feature lets users intuitively identify discrepancies between as-built drawings and actual spatial information.

A representative from Parallel Space stated, “Through CES, the world’s largest exhibition, we aim to showcase our proprietary technologies and products to a diverse audience of countries, regions, businesses, and consumers. Solutions like P-Engine, which have achieved unprecedented automation in 3D spatial data reconstruction, are expected to garner significant interest from global customers and serve as a cornerstone for the digital transformation movement.”

The representative added, “We plan to fully leverage CES to meet with potential buyers, achieve tangible outcomes, and lay the groundwork for entering international markets. In particular, we will actively seek buyers in the U.S., Europe, and Japan.”

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally.
